actions.reason: C0001 has coherent, strong RNA pathway evidence (30/50 significant, large effects) with corroborating continuous CNV signal, supporting a defensible discovery-stage identity. Structure is only weakly supported (near-zero silhouettes, PAC 0.80) and a site/scanner confounder (CJ site, LightSpeed QX/i) is present, but no available evidence request remains and no supported structural revision is indicated, so the candidate is retained for downstream validation with these caveats.

C0002 shows directionally coherent multimodal identity evidence (low CNV burden with depleted CDKN2A/9p/9q/14q losses and inflammation-low RNA pathways) and no set-specific technical confounder. Internal structure is relatively stable (ARI 0.82) but silhouettes are near zero, so structure remains uncertain; no available request or supported structural revision is indicated, so it is retained for downstream validation.

C0003 has only weak, non-significant biological trends and cross-modal support limited mainly to WSI with negative CT/RNA/CNV silhouettes and one patient lacking positive modality support. No set-specific confounder is detected and no available evidence request remains, and no positive structural evidence supports split or merge, so the candidate is retained as a weak discovery-stage candidate for downstream validation.

C0004 has modest biological support (chr10q/PTEN CNV, weak interferon-up RNA trend) and moderate cross-modal consistency across CT/WSI/RNA, but strong technical/site associations (B8/CZ site, SIEMENS scanner, kernel, slice thickness) provide a plausible competing explanation. No available evidence request remains and no supported structural revision is indicated, so it is retained with explicit confounding caveats for downstream validation.

C0005 lacks significant biological signal (small n=11) and shows weak, unstable cross-modal structure (ARI 0.49, PAC 0.67, negative RNA silhouette), though no set-specific confounder is detected. No available evidence request remains and no positive structural evidence supports split or merge, so it is retained as a weak discovery-stage candidate for downstream validation.
